The signal therefore holds 100% exposure (unchanged from 100%), already at the 100% cap, and would add 20% if the index closes above 64 again. rows.answer: Since the start of the standard data window (2021-05-17), SPX had 111 panic-regime days (Panic Index above 64), the last on 2023-03-17. So the edge was concentrated at the one-month horizon and faded by three months. rows.answer: In 2022 for SMH the scipy hindsight labeler found 8 peaks and the causal realtime detector fired 13 signals. The hindsight peaks sit at very high Panic Index levels (91.94 on 2022-05-09, 91.55 on 2022-03-07, 85.31 on 2022-10-12) and are dated at the top of each panic spike. The realtime signals are lower — from 67.97 up to 81.66 — and land a few sessions later, when the index had already retreated 5% from its local max: e.g. 2022-10-13 (79.8) vs. the hindsight 2022-10-12 peak, and repeated re-triggers on 2022-09-28, 2022-10-03, 2022-10-13 and 2022-10-17. The realtime detector also fires more often, clustering within the same selloff rather than labeling one best point. Only the realtime dates are usable for backtests.

rows.answer: Since 2023-01-03 on QQQ, each greed-regime day (Panic Index below 15) cuts exposure by 10%, bounded by 0% and 100%; the what-if run over that window ended at 60% exposure, averaging 29.5%. The signal says the latest 2024-12-31 observation is neutral (Panic Index 47.12, percentile 70) and the action was hold. There were 44 greed days, most recently 2024-03-04. Over this window the upside drag was 167.66pp, against a downside cushion of 133.15pp. Buy & Hold beat the strategy on return, 95.79% versus 42.19%, though the rule had the smaller drawdown (-4.24% vs. -13.56%) and higher Sharpe.
